title.narrative: Phase II Response: A Multi-Sector emergency response for IDP and host communities in South Sudan

description.narrative:
At the onset of the Dec. 2013 conflict crisis, Upper Nile was particularly affected and a large number of people were displaced significant damage on the livelihoods of its people and the town’s infrastructure. Other Counties in Upper Nile State such as Manyo (Kaka, Nown, Athyedhawa etc.), Baliet, Ulang and Nasir were also affected by the clashes. An estimated 15,000 Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) fled to Mabek, Kashaba, Torkuach and Wunriang in Melut County where relative peace and stability has been maintained since the start of the skirmishes. It is here that Caritas Malakal, a strategic partner of CAFOD in Upper Nile state, started an Emergency Response support to IDPs following the on-going conflict crisis in South Sudan. The current intervention is dubbed as the Phase II Emergency Response that will be implemented in neighbouring Manyo County. An assessment conducted by CAFOD and its Partners (Trocaire, NCA, CDoM) in November 2014, showed that there were many IDPs and vulnerable host communities, in Manyo county, whose needs for WASH (water, latrines), NFIs and emergency livelihoods support were entirely un met.
This support to CDoM is in line with one of CAFOD’s key outcomes in its annual operational plan i.e. to support key strategic partners’ to strengthen their capacity. CAFOD’s added value is in its niche in WASH-related aspects.
This project is being financed with additional funding from the Irish Aid and NCA, to support the expansion of Phase I; which was largely done with CAFOD ‘own’ funds and some back donor funds. The funds from NCA, were applied for because the Irish Aid funds could not fully cover the projected budget. So NCA funding was solicited and approved to cover most of the WASH components of the project. NCA and Trocaire (which applied for the Irish funds) will bring in the added value of technical expertise in WASH and protection mainstreaming respectively and capacity strengthening of the Partner; CDoM.
